record.paper_title: Localizing the Vehicle’s Antenna: an Open Problem in 6G Network Sensing
record.context_brief: Control overhead for position-assisted V2I beam management
record.original_question: What is the practical impact, in very dense vehicular networks, of the control-channel overhead required by position-assisted beam management, where a Vehicular Equipment must continuously signal its position information to the Base Station so that the Base Station can use that side information to reduce the beam-search space?

evidence.quote: Of course, the main drawback of sensor-assisted BM approaches is that VE’s position shall be continuously signaled to the BS by means of a proper control channel. Although this is currently considered for vehicular networks in the context of autonomous driving [24], the real impact of control overhead is yet to be determined for very dense vehicular networks.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a millimeter-wave vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) cellular system in which a base station (BS) serves a large population of vehicular user equipments (VEs) using directional beamforming. Initial access and link maintenance are performed by beam management (BM): the BS and each VE must select a pair of transmit/receive beams from finite codebooks of sizes N_BS and N_VE, and the exhaustive search cost scales as N_BS·N_VE. In position-assisted beam management, each VE continuously reports its position (and possibly velocity/orientation) to the BS over a dedicated control channel at update rate f_u (reports per second), with each report consuming B bits; the BS uses this side information to restrict the beam-search to a reduced candidate set of expected size K(σ) ≪ N_BS·N_VE, where σ summarizes the localization uncertainty. Let ρ denote the spatial density of active VEs per cell (vehicles per km^2) and let C_ctrl(ρ, f_u, B) denote the aggregate control-channel overhead (e.g., in bits/s/cell or as a fraction of total radio resources) required to sustain position reporting from all VEs, and let T_BM(ρ, K(σ)) denote the time-frequency resources consumed by the reduced beam search.

Formalize and quantitatively characterize, as a function of vehicle density ρ, update rate f_u, localization uncertainty σ, and codebook sizes N_BS, N_VE, the regime in which the savings T_BM^exhaustive − T_BM(ρ, K(σ)) are outweighed by the control overhead C_ctrl(ρ, f_u, B), in the asymptotic regime of very dense vehicular networks (ρ → ∞). In particular, determine the scaling laws and threshold densities ρ* beyond which position-assisted beam management ceases to provide a net resource benefit over conventional (position-agnostic) beam management.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open practical question: quantifying the control-channel overhead of position-assisted beam management in very dense vehicular networks. Subsequent works on 6G integrated sensing and communication and on sensor/position-aided beam management continue to discuss this trade-off without giving a closed-form characterization of the density threshold, and no definitive solution was found in available sources.
